previous_description: Reusable state machine template for common UX interaction flows, composed of named ExperienceStates and transitions. Canonical examples: 'wizard' — multi-step form with back/next/submit transitions; 'optimistic-update' — loading → success/error with retry; 'tab-panel' — N peer states with tab-driven transitions; 'authenticated-route' — unauthenticated → redirect/login → authenticated.
definition: A reusable, named state machine definition: an ordered set of ExperienceStates and the transitions between them that encodes a recurring interaction flow (e.g. wizard, loading/success/error, tab panel, auth gate). It is not bound to any single View or component and is meant to be applied by several of them.

distinguish_from.when: the symbol represents one state node (e.g. 'loading' or 'step-2') rather than the whole reusable machine that contains it
the symbol is a single trigger→destination edge with an optional guard, not a complete set of states
the reusable thing is one trigger-plus-feedback interaction (e.g. confirm-and-delete) with no states of its own
the states are the top-level, one-off state machine of a single experience rather than a template reused across experiences

code_evidence: A state machine factory or definition (e.g. XState createMachine, a createWizardMachine(steps) function) exported from a shared module and imported by multiple views or components

A generic hook or store (e.g. useAsync, useWizard, useTabs) exposing a finite status union such as 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error' plus transition functions (next, back, retry), reused across features
A shared reducer typed with a discriminated union of states, or a design-system doc page describing the flow and its states (e.g. 'Optimistic update pattern')

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: A plain-text summary of the flow the pattern encodes: its states, the main transitions and the situations it fits. Set it whenever the pattern name alone does not make its behaviour clear.

notes: HTML 5.3 has no state-machine concept; W3C SCXML would be a better reference. The initial state is marked twice, by 'states' ordering and by ExperienceState.initial, so the two can conflict. There is no 'parameters' attribute, though patterns like tab-panel need N. The 'form' and 'multi-step' categories overlap. ExperienceState→specializes→StatePattern is semantically odd. The self-specializes relationship is listed twice.
